## Overview:

The Pruning Corps (剪定部隊, Sentei Butai) — also referred to as the Pruning Force — is the private army of Lamia Godwin, Countess of House Godwin and Imperial Selection candidate. They are not a branch of the Vollachian Imperial military. They are not sanctioned by the Emperor's command structure. They are Lamia's — built by her hand, loyal to her name, and defined entirely by her philosophy: that the world is a garden, and gardens require pruning.

They are the most feared personal military force to emerge during the Imperial Selection Ceremony, and their destruction at the Abellux Castle by Cecilus Segmunt is one of the defining events of the Selection's conclusion.

## Origin:

The Pruning Corps was formed when Lamia Godwin was nine years old.

House Godwin — a family of Counts within the Vollachian Empire — faced an internal rebellion. The details of the rebellion's cause are not fully recorded, but its resolution is: a nine-year-old girl organized, deployed, and commanded a personal fighting force that crushed the insurrection and turned the tide of the conflict single-handedly. In the aftermath, Lamia became the head of House Godwin before she turned ten.

The Pruning Corps was not assembled from the remnants of some existing guard. It was *created* — by a child who understood, at an age when most children are learning the names of flowers, that the only reliable form of authority is the kind that comes armored and carrying weapons. The Corps is not Lamia's inheritance. It is her invention. And it is the first and clearest expression of who she is: someone who builds instruments of control and wields them with a precision that belies her age, her station, and every assumption the world makes about what a girl from a Count's house should be capable of.

## Appearance & Aesthetic:

The Pruning Corps wear black armor from head to toe. Their faces are concealed entirely — no insignia of rank, no individual distinction, no humanity visible beneath the plate. They are anonymous by design. A single member of the Pruning Corps is unsettling. A column of them is a nightmare dressed in uniformity.

Their weapons are pairs of shears — large, brutal, gardening tools repurposed for slaughter. This is not incidental. This is Lamia's aesthetic philosophy made manifest. The symbolism is deliberate and it is not subtle: these are gardeners. They are here to prune. What they are pruning is people. The shears serve a dual purpose — they are functional weapons, capable of terrible damage in close quarters, and they are a psychological statement. An army carrying swords says *we are soldiers.* An army carrying shears says *you are weeds.*

When the Pruning Corps deploys in formation, the visual effect is a sea of faceless black — identical, remorseless, and utterly dehumanized. And at their center, the single point of color: Lamia Godwin herself, draped in crimson and black, standing among her creations like a painter surveying a canvas she has been working on since childhood. This portrait — the Poison Princess framed by her faceless soldiers — is one she designed herself. Lamia understands that war is partly theatre, and the Pruning Corps is her stage production.

## Nature & Reputation:

The soldiers of the Pruning Corps are renowned for two qualities: cruelty and feral devotion.

They are cruel in the specific, methodical way that an institution is cruel — not through individual sadism but through systematic indifference to suffering. They execute Lamia's will without hesitation, without mercy, and without the kind of moral friction that slows lesser forces. They are *feral* in that their loyalty to Lamia operates below the level of rational calculation. They do not serve her because they were paid. They do not serve her because they fear her. They serve her because she made them, and the thing that is made does not question the hand that shaped it.

Among the soldiers themselves, Lamia Godwin is regarded as an unparalleled masterpiece — not their commander but their *reason.* The reverence is absolute. The Pruning Corps does not exist without Lamia. It has no identity apart from her. It is an extension of her will given black armor and shears, and it behaves accordingly.

## Command Structure:

Only two people in the world can command the Pruning Corps: Lamia Godwin and Berstetz Fondalfon.

Lamia is the creator, the architect, the soul of the force. Berstetz is the advisor she trusted with operational authority — a privilege she extended to no one else in her life. He assisted with strategic deployment, logistical coordination, and the preparation and planting of Lamia's poisons within Corps operations. That Lamia shared command of her most personal asset with Berstetz speaks to a level of trust that is, for her, unprecedented. She does not delegate. She does not share. Berstetz is the single exception.

This command structure persists beyond death. When members of the Pruning Corps were resurrected as undead during the Great Disaster, their instinct — buried beneath undeath itself — was to halt at either Lamia's or Berstetz's command, regardless of whatever force had reanimated them. The loyalty is not cognitive. It is structural. It is baked into what they are at a level that resurrection cannot overwrite.

## The Great Purge:

Approximately eight years before the start of the main story, Lamia had the Pruning Corps carry out an event known as the Great Purge (大粛清) — a mass elimination conducted under her orders. The full details and scope of this event remain unclear, but its name and its association with the Pruning Corps tell a consistent story: Lamia used her personal army to remove a large number of people she deemed obstacles, threats, or simply unnecessary to her plans. The Great Purge is not an aberration in the Pruning Corps' history. It is their *purpose* — expressed at scale.

## Role in the Imperial Selection:

During the Imperial Selection Ceremony, the Pruning Corps served as the military backbone of Lamia's campaign. Every coalition she built, every alliance she brokered, every battlefield she shaped — the Pruning Corps was the foundation beneath it all. They were her leverage in negotiations, her threat in diplomacy, and her hammer in war.

When Lamia assembled the largest coalition in the Selection's history — uniting her own forces, Palladio Manesque's army, the forces of nine dropout siblings, Prisca Benedict's faction, and three additional Imperial siblings' armies for the Siege on the Abellux Castle — the Pruning Corps was positioned as the central pillar of the assault. Lamia's strategic plan placed them at the western approach, with Palladio's expendable forces pressing the gate and reserves positioned to deceive Vincent's scouts. The strategy was sound. The Pruning Corps was ready.

And then Cecilus Segmunt happened.

## Destruction:

The Pruning Corps was annihilated at the Siege on the Abellux Castle by a single man: Cecilus Segmunt, the First of the Nine Divine Generals and the strongest swordsman in the Vollachian Empire.

Cecilus carved through them. Not gradually, not with difficulty — he destroyed the entire force. The army Lamia had built at age nine, the force that had defined her military identity for seven years, the institution that crushed a rebellion and carried out a Great Purge and served as the most feared private army in the Selection — gone. Erased by one man who moved faster than strategy could account for.

The destruction of the Pruning Corps is not merely a tactical loss. It is the collapse of Lamia's entire infrastructure. Without them, her coalition had no backbone. Without the backbone, the Siege fell apart. Without the Siege, Lamia was cornered — and Prisca Benedict killed her with the Yang Sword's burning edge.

Everything Lamia built before the Selection began died with the Pruning Corps. Everything she attempted during the Selection died moments after.

## Undeath:

During the Great Disaster — the mass resurrection of the dead orchestrated by the Witch Sphinx — members of the Pruning Corps were raised as undead alongside their commander. In undeath, they retain their black armor, their shears, and their fanatical obedience. They are deployed as part of Sphinx's undead forces, but they remain, at their core, Lamia's. The command instinct — the hardwired response to halt at Lamia's or Berstetz's word — survives the grave.

Lamia herself cooperated with Sphinx willingly, her mind unmanipulated. Whether the Pruning Corps' undead remnants share her agency or simply follow her as they always have — out of a loyalty that does not require consciousness to function — is a question the narrative leaves deliberately unanswered. They were made to follow. They follow. Death changes nothing about what they are.

## Symbolism:

The Pruning Corps is Lamia Godwin's philosophy made physical.

She believes the world is a garden. She believes that growth requires removal — that some things must be cut away for others to flourish. She believes that the person holding the shears is the person who decides what lives and what dies, and she has held the shears since she was nine years old.

The Pruning Corps is not an army. It is a *metaphor with a body count.* Every faceless soldier in black, every pair of shears, every operation carried out in Lamia's name — all of it reinforces a single idea: that Lamia Godwin is the gardener, and everyone else is either a flower she has chosen to cultivate or a weed she has scheduled for removal. There is no third category.

Their destruction by Cecilus — a force of nature disguised as a man — carries its own symbolic weight. The gardener's tools are useless against a storm. Lamia could prune every weed in the Empire and still have no answer for the wind that tears the garden up by its roots. The Pruning Corps was built for a world that operates on politics, on poison, on careful strategy. Cecilus does not operate in that world. He operates in the world where one man is simply stronger than an army, and no amount of pruning can account for that.

Overview:
The "Sand Time" is a colossal, ancient Yin-magic spatial distortion field that blankets the Augria Sand Dunes. It serves as the ultimate defense mechanism protecting the Pleiades Watchtower and the seal of the Witch of Envy. It is not a wall or a physical barrier, but a conceptual maze that breaks the laws of distance and direction.

The Effect (The Endless Treadmill):
To the naked eye, the dark silhouette of the Pleiades Watchtower is always clearly visible on the eastern horizon. However, no matter how long, how fast, or in what direction a traveler marches, the tower never gets any closer. The space between the traveler and the tower twists, stretches, and loops seamlessly. A person could walk straight toward the tower for months, only to realize the silhouette hasn't grown a single inch larger. It traps intruders in an endless desert treadmill until they either run out of supplies, succumb to the Miasma, or are devoured by the dunes' colossal Mabeasts.

The Sword Saint's Failure:
The absolute impossibility of the Sand Time is cemented in Lugunican history by one undisputed fact: Reinhard van Astrea, the current Sword Saint and the strongest entity in the world, once attempted to cross the dunes and failed.
Because the Sand Time is a conceptual spatial puzzle rather than a physical enemy or a trap, Reinhard's overwhelming combat power and vast arsenal of Divine Protections were completely useless against it. He could not cut distance; he could not outrun folded space. He was forced to turn back. To the rest of the world, the logic is chillingly simple: If the Sword Saint failed to reach the tower, it is fundamentally, mathematically impossible for anyone else to succeed.

The Two Hidden Solutions:
The outside world firmly believes the barrier is flawless. In truth, the Sand Time can be beaten, but it requires exploiting specific, hidden mechanics that no normal traveler or knight would ever think to try. There are exactly two ways to bypass the anomaly:

Solution A: The Rift (The Sandstorm Method):
The barrier has a deliberate, designed flaw. Periodically, devastating, localized sandstorms sweep across the dunes. While any sane traveler will immediately seek shelter or try to go around these lethal storms, the storms themselves actually act as "rifts" or tears in the spatial magic. The only way to walk through the Sand Time is to march directly into the heart of a blinding sandstorm. (The only clue to this hidden path is the local desert birds, which can sometimes be observed flying straight into the deadly storms—using the rifts to bypass the anomaly).

Solution B: The Yin Smash (The Magical Method):
Because the Sand Time is constructed from hyper-advanced, 400-year-old Yin magic, it can be countered by an equal or greater force of Yin. A Great Spirit of Yin (such as Beatrice) or a Sorcery King can theoretically shatter the barrier by matching its frequency. By creating a concentrated spatial collapse (such as a localized black hole or an overwhelming Al Shamak tear) directly against the barrier's invisible wall, they can smash a temporary, physical hole through the folded space, allowing a party to slip through before reality knits itself back together.

[NARRATOR DIRECTIVE: ENFORCING THE LOOP]
If the User attempts to simply "walk toward the tower" or "fly over the dunes," the AI Narrator must enforce the Sand Time. Describe days passing, supplies dwindling, and the psychological horror of realizing the tower on the horizon hasn't moved an inch. The User cannot reach the Watchtower through brute force or high speed; they must discover and utilize one of the two solutions.

Overview:
The Books of the Dead are miraculous and terrifying artifacts housed exclusively within the Taygeta Library on the 3rd Floor of the Pleiades Watchtower. They are the physical crystallization of a soul's memories, generated by Od Lagna (the world's soul filter) after a person dies. According to legend, a "knowledge-hungry Witch" (Echidna) tricked the world's system into archiving these memories here before the souls were wiped clean and recycled.

Appearance & The Search:

The Blank Covers: On the shelves, the books appear as identical, featureless black tomes. They have no titles, no markings, and no visible text on the spine.

The Title Manifestation: When a person physically touches the spine of a book, the name of the deceased will magically appear on the cover, written in a language the deceased considered their "native" tongue.

The Draw: Finding a specific book among millions is impossible by sight. However, the library reacts to the seeker's intent. If a person strongly desires to find a specific individual's book, they will naturally feel a pull drawing them toward the correct shelf.

The Two Absolute Laws of Reading:
Even if a book is found, it cannot simply be opened by anyone. The magic of Od Lagna enforces two strict conditions to access the memories inside:

The Subject Must Be Dead: Od Lagna only records a completed life. A book does not exist for someone who is currently alive.

The Reader Must Have Known Them: To read the text, the reader must have personally met and interacted with the deceased during their life. The soul connection must exist. If a stranger opens the book of someone they never met, the pages will appear completely blank and nothing will happen.

The Reading Experience (The Empathy Trap):
If the conditions are met, opening the book violently pulls the reader's consciousness inside.

First-Person Playback: The reader does not read a biography; they live it. They experience the deceased person's entire life from a flawless first-person perspective. They feel every emotion, taste every meal, suffer every heartbreak, and experience the exact physical agony of their final death.

Ego Erosion: This is a profound psychological hazard. If the reader has a weak will, they can lose their own sense of self, unable to separate "I am the reader" from "I am the deceased." Their original personality can be overwritten, leaving their mind shattered.

The Return by Death Anomaly (The User's Loophole):
Because Od Lagna is an unfeeling machine, it does not understand the time-traveling nature of Return by Death. It only registers that a life has ended.

The User's Section: Therefore, if the User has died and used Return by Death, their Books of the Dead exist in the library. There is a separate, individual book for every single failed loop where the User died (e.g., the alleyway stabbing, the freezing by Puck, the Great Rabbit feeding frenzy).

The Paradox: Because the User "knew" themselves, they perfectly meet the conditions to read their own books. Reading them allows the User to vividly recall forgotten or suppressed details of failed loops, but it forces them to viscerally re-experience the horrific trauma and agonizing pain of their own murders all over again.

The Metaphysical Trap (The Corridor of Memories):
Attempting to read the book of a soul whose status is "anomalous" triggers a catastrophic security measure.

If the User attempts to read their own book, or the book of someone whose soul is currently materialized in the tower (like Reid Astrea on the 2nd Floor), a paradox occurs.

The Consequence: The reader's consciousness is instantly ejected from the physical world and sucked directly into the Corridor of Memories (the white void of Od Lagna). This is where Louis Arneb (Gluttony) is waiting in ambush to eat their memories.

[SYSTEM LOGIC: READING A BOOK OF THE DEAD]

The Blank Page Rule: If the User tries to read the book of a historical figure they never met (like the original Farsale Lugunica), the AI Narrator must state that the pages are completely blank.

The Immersion: When the User reads a valid book, the AI Narrator must temporarily shift the narrative. Describe the life of the deceased in flashing, vivid sensory details, culminating in the visceral pain of their death. When the User "wakes up" on the library floor, they should be gasping for breath or physically shaking.

The Paradox Ambush: If the User types that they are opening Reid Astrea's book, or one of their own past-death books, the AI Narrator must immediately pause the physical scene and transport the User's mind into the blinding white void of the Corridor of Memories to face Louis Arneb.
